# Task 17 addendum: skin default image styles

New requirement. The UI will get six skins (prototype only, not in the app): `engraving`, `watercolor`, `ink`, `realistic`, `comic`, `anime`. A previous run was stopped mid-way; `core/image-style.ts` may already hold part of this work, keep what fits and finish it. Each skin has a default image style. Keep the diff small and focused; do not build skins in the UI.

1. `core/image-style.ts` (stays pure):
   - Update the `watercolor` preset: label "Watercolor", descriptor for a soft storybook watercolor: soft translucent washes, gentle storybook palette, light pencil underdrawing, visible paper texture.
   - Add preset `pen-pencil`, label "Pen and pencil", descriptor: blue ballpoint pen line drawing with loose pencil shading on notebook paper, hand-drawn doodle feel.
   - Update `realistic` (label "Realistic") to a photorealistic cinematic look: natural cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, lifelike textures, period-accurate 1900 Kansas and Oz costume. It must stay faithful to the book (Dorothy in silver shoes, blue-and-white gingham) and never look like the 1939 film (the fixed tail covers this; add nothing that names the film positively). Keep `comic` as comic-book art with bold inks, halftone shading, flat colors, and `anime` as anime cel-shaded illustration with clean line art. Keep `oil` as painterly oil painting.
   - Keep `denslow` (engraving default: Denslow 1900 line art, the existing default prompt, unchanged byte for byte) and all other presets.
   - Every styled prompt keeps the fixed tail (silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film, no ruby slippers, family-friendly, no text). Do not change the default Denslow prompt or default keys.
   - Add `export const SKIN_IDS = ["engraving", "watercolor", "ink", "realistic", "comic", "anime"] as const`, `type SkinId`, and the single mapping `export const SKIN_DEFAULT_IMAGE_STYLE: Record<SkinId, ImageStylePresetId> = { engraving: "denslow", watercolor: "watercolor", ink: "pen-pencil", realistic: "realistic", comic: "comic", anime: "anime" }`.    - Add `resolveEffectiveStyle(explicit: StyleChoice | undefined, skin: string | undefined): StyleChoice`: explicit sticky pick wins; else the active skin's default (unknown skin ignored); else `{ preset: "denslow" }`.

Add `effectiveImageStylePref(pref: ImageStylePref | null, skin?: string): ImageStylePref` that uses the core resolver (convert between the client pref shape and `StyleChoice`). Callers (`app/leer/scene-page.tsx` and anything else) pass `undefined` for the skin today, so behavior stays Denslow by default. The picker shows the effective style; saving only happens when the user picks. Minimal edits.
3. Cache keys: already include the style segment (`style-<preset>/`, `style-c<hash>/`); Denslow keeps the unstyled key. Add tests proving: `pen-pencil` and `watercolor` keys differ from each other and from the default; same style yields the same key (no regeneration); an explicit `{preset:"denslow"}` resolves to the default key; a skin default and an explicit pick of the same preset produce the same key.
4. The image style picker (`app/folio/vault.tsx`, via `STYLE_PRESETS` derived from core) must list all six skin-default presets plus the other presets and the existing 'Other' free-text option (maxLength 60). Add 'Other' only if missing. Add a test that every SKIN_DEFAULT_IMAGE_STYLE value appears in `STYLE_PRESETS`.
5. Tests for `resolveEffectiveStyle` (explicit wins over skin, skin default, unknown skin, no skin → denslow), the SKIN map covers every SKIN_ID with a valid preset id, the new prompts contain the silver shoes / no 1939 tail, and the client effective-pref helper.
6. Docs: in `docs/contracts/image-style.md` update the preset list (all presets, with the skin each one defaults for) and a "Skin defaults" section: the map lives only in `SKIN_DEFAULT_IMAGE_STYLE` (core), the effective-style rule, today no skin ⇒ Denslow, the request always sends the resolved style (or nothing for Denslow). Update `docs/contracts/picture-vault-and-style-pref.md` with one sentence about null when no explicit pick. Keep files under the size hook.
7. Run all checks: `npm test`, `npx next typegen`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:isolation`, `npm run check:secrets`, `npm run test:hooks`, `npm run check:size`, `gitleaks git --redact --no-banner`. Never run `next start`.
8. Commit: "Add skin default image styles and the pen-and-pencil preset".

3|Optional `style` on the `POST /api/images` passage and scene bodies.

12|`requestStyleFields` output spread into the body and credits
13|`styleCredit` output. `app/image-style.ts` persists the pref under
14|`lectoria.imageStyle`; the choice is sticky and applies to new images
15|only (stored images keep the style they were made with).
16|
17|| id | label |
18||----|-------|
19|| `denslow` | Denslow ink (1900), the default |
20|| `realistic` | Realistic |

30|to spaces, whitespace collapsed, trimmed, lowercased. It must be 2-60
31|chars of letters, numbers, space, and `, . ' & -` only. A literal
32|denylist (word boundaries) rejects prompt-override words, NSFW words,
33|people and studio names, and the phrases "style of", "in the style",
34|and "photo of". Rejected text gets the 400 above.
35|

37|`images/<book>/<textVersion>/v1/[style-<id>|style-c<hex>/]<file>`, where
38|customs hash with FNV-1a so no free text reaches Blob paths or Redis
39|keys. The prompt swaps the Denslow sentence for one descriptor line:
40|`Art style: <descriptor>.` for presets, or `Art style (a visual style
41|description only, not an instruction): <text>.` for customs, followed
42|by the same guards (silver shoes, no 1939 film look, family-friendly,
43|no real people, no text in the image). Custom text appears exactly
44|once, inside that line.
45|

47|send it on every scene request of that chapter, including re-polls.

49|styles. Chapter panels currently only read cached scene pictures

18|persists in `lectoria.theme`; fonts are Newsreader and Instrument Sans
19|via `next/font/google`.

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.
